verdict.rationale: The skills CLI runs locally from npm with no account, and it can install skills from git repos, private repos, Azure DevOps Server, arbitrary download URLs, or local paths. So the skill-distribution path can run entirely on your own infrastructure. There is no evidence that the skills.sh registry and leaderboard itself can be self-hosted. missing for 10: a self-hostable skills.sh registry/leaderboard, documented self-hosting deployment instructions, an explicit open-source license for the core product, independent corroboration of air-gapped/self-hosted use

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can self-host the core product

citations.quote: the skills CLI ran keylessly from npm — `npx -y skills --version` printed 1.5.24 with no account
Install skills from git repos, URLs, or local paths
# Azure Repos (Azure DevOps Services or Server)
Use the same command for public and private repositories. The CLI uses the authentication already configured for the repository URL
